terms.title: Salmon Wallet Terms and Conditions with Power-ups
terms.markdown:
These terms describe the use of Salmon Wallet as a self-custodial wallet and its optional Payments, Swap and SKR features.

**Power-ups version 1.5.**

## 1 Who we are and scope of the agreement

These Terms and Conditions (the **“Terms”**) govern the relationship between you and **GeekOcean Labs Ltd**, a company incorporated in the British Virgin Islands (**“Salmon,” “we,” “us,”** or **“our”**).

They apply to the Salmon Wallet mobile applications and browser extension (the **“Wallet”**), the features we provide through them, and the institutional website [salmonwallet.io](https://www.salmonwallet.io) (together, the **“Services”**). The institutional website provides information about Salmon; it is not a web wallet.

By accepting these Terms or using the Services to which they apply, you accept this agreement. If you act on behalf of an entity, you represent that you have authority to bind it. If you do not accept the agreement, do not use those Services.

The [Power-ups Privacy Policy](/privacy) explains how information is processed. Accepting these Terms does not replace any specific consent required for optional data processing.

## 2 Eligibility and availability

You must be at least eighteen, have reached the age of majority where you live, and have capacity to enter into this agreement. You must be legally able to use the requested feature where you are located and comply with restrictions applicable to your residence, incorporation, or other relevant criteria.

You may not use the Services in breach of applicable sanctions or restrictions, or to launder assets, finance unlawful activities, defraud others, or infringe third-party rights. You may not act on behalf of a person or entity prohibited from accessing the feature.

Availability depends on the feature, network, asset, platform, location, and provider. Being able to download the Wallet does not mean that all its features are available or permitted in every country or region. An indication of availability does not certify the user's personal legal position.

Salmon may restrict a feature when necessary to comply with law, apply provider conditions, protect security, or respond to a valid order. Territorial conditions for Swap are detailed in section 7.

## 3 Nature of the service and core features

Salmon develops and provides self-custodial software: the user retains the keys that authorize movements of assets recorded on a blockchain, a network that maintains a shared transaction record. The Wallet allows users to consult and interact with that record; assets are not deposited in an account managed by Salmon.

The core features of this version allow users to create or import a wallet, view balances and public activity, receive and send Solana digital assets, and view supported collectibles, including NFTs, which are individually identifiable tokens, and send or burn them. Burning permanently destroys the token. They also allow users to view Bitcoin balances and history and send and receive BTC on the Bitcoin network. The Wallet displays the transfer features available for each network and asset.

The Wallet also connects to decentralized applications (**“dApps”**, applications that run on a blockchain) when you choose to: in the browser extension through the Wallet Standard, and on Android through Mobile Wallet Adapter, two open connection standards. It signs messages and sign-in requests for them when you approve. It displays staking positions it reads from the network, such as Staked SOL accounts and SKR positions; this view is read-only.

**Bitcoin is limited to viewing information, sending, and receiving; it is not part of Swap or the Payments Power-up.** Payments and Swap operate only on Solana. This version does not enable Ethereum connections or transactions.

In addition to these features, users may use the available Power-ups, subject to section 5 and their specific conditions.

Salmon provides the interface and software connecting users to network information and third-party tools. For Swap, Salmon selects the available provider according to applicable restrictions, requests and presents quotes, and prepares instructions for the user to decide whether to authorize them. The routing provider supplies quoting and routing software; blockchain protocols process the authorized exchange. Section 7 describes these roles separately.

Salmon does not operate its own trading market, maintain an order book, or act as buyer, seller, or counterparty to swaps. It does not hold funds in custody, accept deposits for management, or possess the keys needed to transact for the user. Receiving a fee for use of its integration does not give it control over the assets the user exchanges.

This version does not include cross-network transfers through bridges, buying or selling with bank money or cards, staking transactions, loans, derivatives, or prediction markets. Payments does not include x402 or encrypted messaging. References to future products in marketing materials do not enable those features or guarantee their launch.

## 4 Keys and transaction authorization

The private keys, recovery phrase, and local password protecting the Wallet remain under your control. The Wallet stores the keys and phrase encrypted on your device; Salmon's servers do not receive, store, or have the ability to reconstruct them. On a Solana Seeker phone, a wallet can instead be kept in the device's Seed Vault, the phone's protected key storage; its keys stay in the Seed Vault, and Salmon's servers do not receive them either.

Salmon does not create a custodial account or issue credentials through which it can restore your access. If you lose the means needed to access or restore your wallet, Salmon cannot recover them or your funds.

Requesting a quote, activating a Power-up, or creating a payment request does not authorize Salmon to move assets. Every transaction requiring a signature must be authorized by you using your keys. For the Bitcoin transfers and Solana transfers, payments, and swaps described here, signing takes place on your device, and the signed transaction is sent directly from it to the network connection provider. It does not pass through Salmon's servers for broadcasting. Preparing or simulating unsigned instructions does not allow Salmon to create a signature for you or decide on transactions with your funds.

Before signing, review the network, asset, recipient, amount, fees, permissions, and expected outcome. Do not sign a request you do not understand. Authorization granted to a network program may have effects different from a simple transfer.

Salmon may limit access to its own interface, but doing so does not allow it to freeze your assets, modify a confirmed transaction, or restore your keys. Certain token issuers and external programs may have their own powers or restrictions, independent of Salmon.

Protect your device and keep a secure backup of your recovery phrase. Do not include it in payment requests or support messages. Salmon will never ask for that phrase or a private key by email, messaging, or social media.

## 5 General Power-up conditions

### 5.1 What they are and how to use them

Power-ups are optional features integrated into the Wallet that extend specific tasks. The “+” button opens the catalog, where you can enable or disable features available for your version and location using their respective controls. Activation displays the feature's tools; it does not sign a transaction or grant general authorization to transact with your assets.

Activating Payments or Swap does not require buying tokens, points, a subscription, or an additional license. Free activation does not exclude fees for a particular transaction, such as the Swap fee and network costs described in section 10.

The SKR Power-up is read-only: it shows a Seeker owner's SKR staking position in a tab of the Wallet. It does not stake, unstake, or move assets.

The Power-ups covered by these Terms are features integrated by Salmon. They are not an open marketplace of programs that third parties can freely install or update in the Wallet.

### 5.2 Specific information and providers

Each Power-up is subject to these Terms, its specific section, and the notices presented before use. The interface identifies the external provider involved where applicable, and the section of these Terms covering the feature links to that provider's conditions. The data needed for the feature is described in the Privacy Policy.

Salmon's integration code and the external service perform different roles. Identifying an external provider does not remove Salmon's legal obligations for its own software, information, or conduct. Nor does it make Salmon a custodian or counterparty to transactions the user performs with that provider or network programs.

### 5.3 Deactivation and changes

Disabling a Power-up prevents its use through that Wallet feature, but does not cancel a broadcast transaction, erase the public record, or automatically revoke permissions granted to external programs. Deleting local data and disabling a feature are different actions.

Salmon may withdraw or limit a Power-up for security, provider availability, or compliance reasons. No feature is guaranteed indefinitely. Adding other features requires describing their operation, conditions, and data processing before making them available; this clause does not authorize unspecified future services.

## 6 Payments and payment requests

### 6.1 Purpose of the tool

Payments allows users to create requests on their device to receive an amount of USDC, a token whose issuer seeks to maintain a value equivalent to the US dollar, on Solana. It uses Solana Pay, a payment-instruction format that can be shared as a QR code or text and opened in a compatible wallet.

The request identifies the recipient, token, amount, and a reference used to look for the payment on the network. The shared QR code or text also includes the account name, order identifier, and any note you add. You can set an expiry time to organize the request. Creating a request does not move funds or oblige its recipient to pay.

The payer reviews and authorizes a transfer using their own wallet. In Salmon, scanning a compatible request fills in the transfer fields but does not automatically sign or execute it. Activating Payments is not required to use the core sending feature to pay a compatible request.

### 6.2 Relationship between payer and payee

Payment is made from the payer's address to the recipient's address. Salmon does not receive the amount for onward delivery to the recipient, hold it in escrow, or provide a guarantee, commercial arbitration, or payment-refund service.

The existence, lawfulness, and performance of the obligation behind the payment are the parties' responsibility. A request, note, or payment status shown in the Wallet is not a tax invoice issued by Salmon or a guarantee of the recipient's identity or delivery of goods or services.

Claims about the commercial relationship or a refund must be directed to the counterparty. Salmon handles problems with its software without thereby assuming the commercial obligations of the payer or recipient.

### 6.3 Confirmation, expiry, and retention

A QR code, screenshot, or transaction identifier does not by itself prove that payment is confirmed. The Wallet searches the network for a finalized transfer matching the requested reference, token, recipient, and amount. If a transfer does not match, it may not be automatically linked to the request even if movements appear in Activity.

Expiry organizes the request within the Wallet; it does not technically invalidate the code or prevent someone from sending funds later. Deleting a request stops displaying and tracking that local record, but does not prevent receipt of funds at the address or erase payments recorded on the blockchain.

Requests are stored on the device where they are created, and removing a wallet from the app or disabling Payments does not delete them. They are not synchronized through a Salmon account and may be lost when application data is deleted or the device is reset. Recovering the keys does not necessarily restore local notes and requests.

### 6.4 Notes and privacy

Content shared in the QR code or text is not an end-to-end encrypted communication. Anyone with access to the code can read and copy its data, including the account name and note. Salmon does not receive or store the request list or its notes on its servers.

In Salmon's Payments flow, the note is not included in the transaction or published on the blockchain. Payment data, the order identifier, and a single-use reference are recorded. A QR recipient may retain or disclose its content outside Salmon; do not include confidential information, keys, identity documents, or other people's data without authorization.

Payments does not automatically convert assets, use x402, or allow purchases of Salmon features. Salmon charges no fee of its own to create requests or receive their payments; sending may incur network costs.

## 7 Swap and routing providers

### 7.1 What Salmon does

Swap allows users to prepare an exchange of one token for another within Solana; it does not allow swapping BTC on Bitcoin or moving assets between Bitcoin and Solana. Participants have different roles:

- **Salmon** provides the interface and integration software. It receives your request, applies availability controls, queries the routing provider, and prepares and simulates an unsigned transaction. It presents the quote and transaction details for your review.
- **The routing provider**, such as 0x or Metis, supplies software that queries and combines options across liquidity sources: programs and participants that enable asset exchanges. It returns a quote, a route, and instructions to prepare the transaction. It does not receive your private keys from Salmon.
- **You** choose the assets and amount, decide whether to accept the conditions, and authorize signing on your device. The device sends the signed transaction directly to the network connection provider; Salmon's servers do not receive it for rebroadcasting.
- **The Solana network and the protocols in the route** process the transaction under their rules and the signed instructions. The exchange is recorded on the blockchain, not in a Salmon custodial account.

Preparing and simulating a transaction does not move your funds or constitute an order that Salmon can execute on its own. Salmon does not receive assets to exchange on your behalf, act as counterparty, or exercise discretion over transactions with your funds. It may limit access to its interface or preparation of a quote, but cannot modify a signed transaction to dispose of your assets without fresh valid authorization.

### 7.2 Providers and territorial access

The providers integrated for this feature are **0x** and **Metis**, the Jupiter routing software used by Salmon. **Swap is not offered in Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, the United Kingdom, mainland China, Myanmar, Côte d’Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Iraq, Libya, Mali, Nicaragua, Somalia, Sudan, Yemen, Zimbabwe, or the Crimea, Sevastopol, Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions of Ukraine.** **Eligible requests from the United States, Singapore and Taiwan are directed to 0x, not Metis.** **If the country of the connection cannot be determined, Swap is not offered.** In every other country or region, eligible requests are directed to Metis, selected according to its service's territorial restrictions and the requirements applicable to the integration. This selection does not enable products other than the identified service or represent a statement of third-party regulatory permissions.

The confirmation screen names the quote provider before signing. Salmon may add or replace providers; before you use a new integration, the interface names its provider and these Terms link to its conditions. Changing providers cannot be used to evade a prohibition applicable to the user or activity.

To determine availability and select a provider, Salmon estimates the country from the IP address, which identifies the internet connection. This check does not use the device's GPS or establish citizenship or residence. Applicable distribution and service restrictions also apply. Where the application was downloaded does not, by itself, establish user eligibility, and having the Wallet does not guarantee access to Swap. Additional restrictions may apply based on residence, sanctions, wallet address, asset, or provider requirements.

If no enabled provider can legally and technically serve the request, Swap is not offered for that request. You must not hide your location or use a VPN, proxy, or other means to bypass a restriction. If you believe a territorial decision is incorrect, you may contact support; access to the feature is not guaranteed.

Restricting Swap does not give Salmon control over your assets. Core features remain subject to their own availability conditions.

### 7.3 Provider conditions

In addition to these Terms, the conditions of an external service you interact with may apply, according to their scope. You can consult the [0x terms](https://0x.org/legal/terms-of-service) and [Jupiter's published terms](https://developers.jup.ag/docs/legal/terms-of-use). Salmon's integration is itself subject to the software-access agreements of [0x](https://0x.org/legal/api-license-agreement) and [Jupiter/Metis](https://developers.jup.ag/docs/legal/sdk-api-license-agreement). Those agreements govern Salmon's access to the provider; they do not make the user a party to commercial obligations assumed solely by Salmon.

Salmon obtains these services through their online channels under the standard conditions applicable to the chosen service and plan, without individually negotiated agreements. The confirmation screen names the specific service, and its conditions are the ones linked in this section. Terms for a different product from the same provider do not authorize its use.

The provider may reject a quote because of access restrictions, address checks, lack of liquidity, or technical limitations. An available quote does not certify a token's lawfulness, authenticity, or safety, or replace restrictions that must be observed.

### 7.4 Quotes and outcomes

Quotes are temporary. Prices and costs may change between the query and confirmation. A route may use several liquidity sources and does not guarantee the best price across all market alternatives.

The difference between the quoted price and the outcome is called slippage. Before signing, review the estimated amount, minimum amount you accept receiving, applicable tolerance, assets, and fees. If a quote expires, request a new one. A transaction may be rejected or fail; risks and network costs may exist even if the exchange is not completed.

Displaying a route, ranking options, or applying a technical setting does not constitute investment advice or a guarantee of returns or best execution. Do not interpret an asset's presence as a recommendation by Salmon.

### 7.5 Signing, fees, and cancellation

The fees described in section 10 are incorporated into the transaction presented for your authorization. Salmon may receive its fee without being the recipient of the assets exchanged on the user's behalf.

Before signing, you may abandon the transaction. After broadcasting, closing the application or disabling Swap does not cancel it. Salmon cannot alter a confirmed transaction or unilaterally refund funds or charges received by third parties.

## 8 External information and services

Salmon uses technical providers to query balances and activity, obtain asset data, and connect the Wallet to public networks. A network connection provider allows users to query the blockchain and broadcast a signed transaction; that role does not make it custodian of your keys.

Prices, metadata, images, and other content may be incomplete, delayed, false, or malicious. A name, logo, valuation, or label does not establish an asset's authenticity or rights over the work or property it claims to represent. Viewing or receiving an NFT does not grant a license to its content unless the rights holder grants one.

Independent third parties apply their own terms and policies. Salmon may select or replace them for operational, commercial, security, or compliance reasons. That selection does not guarantee they are free of faults, but neither does it exclude Salmon's own responsibilities that the law does not allow it to transfer.

## 9 Networks and transaction risks

Acceptance, ordering, and confirmation of a transaction depend on the network and its programs, not on Salmon's discretionary approval. A confirmed transaction may be irreversible. Burning an NFT permanently destroys it and cannot be undone. Sending to an incorrect or incompatible address can cause permanent loss.

Digital assets may lose all value. Their issuers may impose restrictions; Salmon does not guarantee the stability of tokens intended to maintain a stable value, such as USDC. Networks, programs, and providers may suffer congestion, errors, attacks, outages, or changes affecting transactions.

A program executable on a blockchain, also called a smart contract, may contain vulnerabilities even if its code is public or has been reviewed. Simulation and risk notices are aids, not security guarantees. No interface eliminates the risks of signing a transaction.

## 10 Fees and costs

### 10.1 Core features and Payments

Salmon charges no fee of its own to create or import a wallet, view balances or activity, send or receive assets, display collectibles, or activate the Power-ups covered by these Terms. Nor does it charge its own fee to create Payments requests or receive their payments.

### 10.2 Swap fee

Salmon's standard Swap fee is **0.5%**, unless a lower rate or exemption is shown before signing. The confirmation screen must indicate the rate, amount, token charged, and whether it is deducted from the asset sent or received. Review the estimated net amount to avoid confusing the exchange value with what you will receive after charges.

The fee is incorporated into the transaction you authorize and is received at a Salmon address when the transaction containing it executes. Requesting a quote and abandoning it without signing does not incur Salmon's Swap fee.

On some token pairs, 0x charges its own fee of up to **0.15%**, already included in the quoted amount you receive and separate from Salmon's fee and network costs. Liquidity sources may incorporate their own charges into the quote. Charges communicated by the provider must be reflected in the presented breakdown, indicating whether they are included in the price. Do not interpret Salmon's fee as the total transaction cost.

In addition, under the Standard plan used by Salmon, **0x collects trade surplus**, or positive slippage: the favorable difference that may arise when a transaction executes at a better price than quoted. This collection follows 0x's terms and mechanism, is separate from its 0.15% fee, and is not Salmon revenue. Therefore, not all price improvement is guaranteed to be passed on to the user. Before signing, you must be informed of this treatment along with the estimated net amount and minimum amount you accept receiving; the exact surplus, if any, depends on execution.

Payments Salmon makes for access to third-party tools or infrastructure do not, by themselves, become a subscription or additional user charge. Any transaction charge to the user must correspond to the conditions presented before signing.

### 10.3 Network costs and changes

Sending assets or interacting with programs may require network processing fees and, in certain cases, funds to create accounts needed to receive tokens. These amounts are not Salmon revenue merely because they appear in the confirmation.

Network costs are estimates and may vary. The network may charge for processing a failed transaction. Costs actually received by the network or third parties cannot be unilaterally refunded by Salmon, without prejudice to applicable legal rights.

Salmon will disclose changes to its rate before they apply to new transactions. No change authorizes charges against your funds without a transaction you decide to sign.

## 11 Financial information and user obligations

Salmon provides technological tools, not financial, tax, legal, or investment advice. It does not manage a portfolio for you, accept a mandate to transact, or promise returns, liquidity, or a particular price.

Describing Salmon as a self-custodial software provider rather than the operator of an exchange, bank, custodian, or broker reflects the functions described in these Terms. It does not exclude obligations or classifications that mandatory law applies to a specific activity. Using an external provider does not transfer a license to Salmon or replace the obligations of each participant.

You determine and meet the tax obligations arising from your transactions. Salmon does not withhold or report taxes on the user's behalf through these features.

## 12 Acceptable use and controls

You must not use the Services for unlawful activities, fraud, market manipulation, sanctions evasion, unauthorized access, introduction of malicious code, or interference harming others or the infrastructure. You must not falsify eligibility information or bypass availability controls.

Salmon and its providers may check public addresses against sanctions and risk information to decide whether to allow access to a feature. These controls do not grant access to your keys or amount to full identity verification. An alert may prevent a transaction through the interface without enabling Salmon to freeze funds on the network.

Identity documents are not requested to create or import the Wallet. If a service requires additional information to satisfy its conditions or the law, you must be told who requests it and for what purpose before providing it. Access to a feature is not guaranteed when its requirements cannot be met.

## 13 Intellectual property and open source

Salmon's own brands, texts, images, and designs are protected by applicable rights. You may not use them to suggest a nonexistent association, authorization, or endorsement.

The Wallet's published source code is offered under Apache License 2.0, with the notices and licenses applicable to its components. That license controls the rights to use, modify, and distribute the code that it grants. It does not grant trademark rights or unlimited access to third-party infrastructure or services.

Salmon does not warrant or support modified versions independently distributed by third parties. An external modification does not make that third party Salmon's representative.

For suggestions you voluntarily provide and have the right to share, you grant Salmon a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use and adapt them. That authorization does not allow disclosure of personal information beyond what is described in the Privacy Policy.

To report intellectual-property infringement, contact [help@salmonwallet.io](mailto:help@salmonwallet.io) and identify the work, disputed content, its location, and the basis of your claim.

## 14 Availability and warranties

To the extent permitted by law, the Services are offered as available and without guarantees of uninterrupted operation, absence of errors, absolute security, or compatibility with every asset, network, or device.

Salmon does not guarantee transaction confirmation, accuracy of third-party data, or recovery of keys or assets. These exclusions do not limit mandatory statutory warranties or rights.

## 15 Liability

Each participant is responsible for its own obligations. User decisions, network rules, and third-party actions do not automatically become Salmon's obligations through use of its interface.

To the maximum extent permitted by law, Salmon and its representatives are not liable for indirect, incidental, special, or consequential damage, lost profits or opportunities, or losses arising from events beyond their reasonable control. Salmon's total aggregate liability relating to the Services is limited to the greater of the fees it received from you during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim or USD 100.

These limitations do not exclude liability for fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, or other conduct or harm for which liability cannot legally be limited. They do not remove mandatory consumer rights or Salmon's own data-protection obligations.

## 16 Third-party claims arising from unlawful use

To the extent permitted by law, you will be responsible for third-party claims and reasonable expenses you cause through unlawful or abusive use of the Services, infringement of others' rights, or a breach of these Terms attributable to you. This obligation does not cover losses caused by Salmon's conduct or restrict the user's non-waivable defenses or rights.

## 17 Suspension and termination

You may stop using the Services and disable Power-ups. Before deleting the Wallet, make sure you retain the means to recover your keys and any local records you need.

Salmon may limit or suspend components under its control because of breaches, security risks, legal requirements, or provider unavailability. Where possible and legally permitted, it will explain the reason and available options.

Suspending an interface does not by itself change control of the keys or the blockchain asset record. You may use software compatible with your keys and networks, subject to its terms and restrictions. Suspension does not reverse transactions or erase data that must legally be retained.

## 18 Versions and changes

These Terms are identified by version and effective date. The features covered are those enabled in the application to which that version applies. Publishing a draft does not make it an effective agreement or activate a feature.

Salmon may update the Terms to reflect service changes or legal requirements. Material changes will be communicated with reasonable advance notice unless a legal requirement or urgent risk justifies a different period. We will request acceptance when required and will not apply changes retroactively to reduce accrued rights.

If you do not accept a change, you may stop using the affected feature. Provisions concerning completed transactions, liability, and disputes survive as applicable. The conditions governing a transaction are determined by the version effective for it, not by deletion of a file or link.

## 19 Governing law and dispute resolution

These Terms are governed by the laws of the British Virgin Islands. To the extent permitted by law, its courts will hear disputes relating to the Services.

This choice does not deprive consumers of mandatory protections where they reside or their legal right to approach the courts or authorities available to them. You may first contact support to try to resolve an issue, without limiting available legal deadlines or remedies.

If you obtain the Wallet through Apple App Store, you contract for Salmon's service with GeekOcean Labs Ltd, not Apple. Salmon is responsible for its application, content, and support; Apple is not obliged to maintain or support the Wallet.

You must use it on devices you own or control in accordance with Apple's rules, including permitted shared uses. Open-source licenses retain their own scope.

To the extent required by Apple's conditions, Salmon handles claims relating to the application, compliance, and intellectual property. If the application fails to meet an applicable warranty, you may notify Apple and request a refund of its purchase price, if any, under Apple's rules; this does not make Apple responsible for digital-asset transactions. Apple and its subsidiaries are third-party beneficiaries of the provisions applicable to the application and may enforce them.

When you download the Wallet from Google Play or an extension store, that store's rules also apply. Distribution does not mean the store operator holds funds in custody or guarantees assets, providers, quotes, or transactions.

For questions about these Terms or Wallet problems, write to [help@salmonwallet.io](mailto:help@salmonwallet.io). The operator is GeekOcean Labs Ltd, British Virgin Islands. Do not include private keys or recovery phrases in your communication.

privacy.markdown:
This policy explains what information is used in Salmon Wallet and its Payments, Swap and SKR Power-ups, who receives it, and what choices you can make.

**Power-ups version 1.5.**

## 1 Controller and scope

**GeekOcean Labs Ltd**, a company incorporated in the British Virgin Islands (**“Salmon,” “we,” “us,”** or **“our”**), is the controller for the information processing it carries out for the purposes described in this Policy.

The Policy covers the Salmon Wallet mobile applications and browser extension (the **“Wallet”**), their features, and the institutional website [salmonwallet.io](https://www.salmonwallet.io) (the **“Site”**). The Site provides information; it is not a web wallet.

The core features covered by this version include Solana and viewing balances and history, sending, and receiving BTC on the Bitcoin network. **Payments and Swap operate only on Solana; Bitcoin is not part of those Power-ups.** Ethereum connections and transactions are not enabled. Payments covers payment requests through Solana Pay; it does not include x402 or encrypted messaging.

The Wallet also connects to decentralized applications (**“dApps”**, applications that run on a blockchain) when you choose to: in the browser extension through the Wallet Standard, and on Android through Mobile Wallet Adapter, two open connection standards. On Solana Seeker phones, a wallet can be kept in the device's Seed Vault, the phone's protected key storage. The Wallet also displays staking positions it reads from the network, including those of the **SKR Power-up**, which is read-only: it shows a Seeker owner's SKR staking position and does not stake, unstake, or move funds.

The [Power-ups Terms and Conditions](/terms) describe the service. This Policy is a data notice: reading it or accepting the Terms does not by itself constitute consent to analytics or other optional processing.

For privacy questions or to exercise your rights, write to [help@salmonwallet.io](mailto:help@salmonwallet.io).

## 2 Self-custody and privacy limitations

Salmon is a self-custodial wallet: you control the keys that authorize movements of your assets. The Wallet stores your private keys and recovery phrase encrypted on your device. Salmon's servers do not receive or store those secrets or the local password protecting the Wallet and cannot reconstruct them. On a Solana Seeker phone, the keys of a wallet kept in the Seed Vault stay in the device's Seed Vault instead of the Wallet's own encrypted storage; Salmon's servers do not receive them in either case.

Creating or importing a wallet does not require a Salmon account, email address, name, or identity documents. Activating a Power-up does not transfer control of those keys to Salmon.

Self-custody does not mean anonymity or absence of data processing. Wallet addresses, queries, IP addresses—identifiers of internet connections—and transactions may allow a person to be identified or linked to information. We treat information as personal data where it qualifies under the law, even if it comes from a public record.

The blockchain maintains an independent public record. Salmon cannot erase your transactions or prevent third parties from viewing, copying, or analyzing them.

## 3 Information that remains on your device

### Keys, preferences, and authorizations

In addition to keys, the Wallet retains local preferences, including Power-up activation and analytics choices. Selecting a feature may require checking its availability with Salmon; it does not mean that all local data is sent to the server.

Transactions are signed on the device. A signed transaction contains instructions and cryptographic proof of authorization, but does not contain the private key or recovery phrase.

### Biometrics and camera

If you enable biometric unlock in the mobile app, the operating system performs the check and communicates the result to the Wallet. So that you do not have to type it, the Wallet then keeps its local password on the device, sealed with a key that the operating system releases only after a successful check; that password never leaves the device. Salmon does not receive your fingerprint, face, or biometric template.

With your permission, the mobile app uses the camera to read QR codes. Image analysis takes place on the device; the image is not sent to Salmon as part of scanning. Data extracted from the code, such as an address or amount, may subsequently be used to query the network or prepare a transaction, as explained in this Policy.

### Payments requests

Requests created through Payments are stored locally by wallet and network. They include the recipient, USDC amount—a token whose issuer seeks to maintain a value equivalent to the US dollar—order identifier, reference, any note you add, and expiry; once a request is paid, the Wallet also stores the payer's address and the signature of the transaction it found on the network. The shared payment code also includes the account name. The request list and notes are not sent to Salmon's servers or synchronized between devices through this Power-up, and they are kept in the app's storage without the encryption that protects keys.

Deleting a request erases that local record. Removing a wallet from the app or disabling Payments does not delete its requests; uninstalling the app or erasing its data does. Keeping the recovery phrase allows keys to be restored, but not necessarily those local records.

## 4 Data we receive or query

### Support and communications

When you contact us, we receive your email address, message, and any files or data you choose to send. If you include a wallet address or transaction, we may associate it with that communication to handle it. We do not automatically obtain your email address when you create the Wallet.

We use **Migadu** to host and manage support emails, including messages and attachments. Salmon's team manually deletes those emails according to the period in section 9.

Do not send private keys or recovery phrases. If you need to demonstrate control of a wallet for a request, we will not ask you to reveal those secrets or make a payment.

### Public network information

The Wallet and supporting infrastructure query public addresses, balances, transactions, public signatures, asset identifiers, and collectible data to display contents and activity. An address is a wallet's public identifier, not a secret credential. The Wallet also reads the staking positions of an address, such as Staked SOL accounts and SKR positions; that query sends the public address to Salmon's infrastructure and to Triton One as in other queries, and the view is read-only.

When a dApp asks the browser extension to connect or sign and you have accepted analytics, the extension sends that dApp's web address to Salmon's servers, which fetch the dApp's public page to read its name and icon for the approval screen; the extension then loads that icon from the host the page names, which receives the device IP address. Without analytics consent, the extension sends nothing about the dApp and shows only its web address. When a dApp asks the Android app to connect or sign through Mobile Wallet Adapter, the device itself contacts the dApp's website to check its identity (its Digital Asset Links file) and, once approved, to load its icon; that site receives the device IP address.

Data associated with an NFT, an individually identifiable token, may include images, descriptions, and links hosted outside the blockchain. Retrieving that content may reveal the requested identifier and the querying party's IP address to its hosting server.

### Requests and technical logs

Communicating with our infrastructure involves processing information needed to respond and protect the service. Request logs record the IP address, date and time, the type of request and the web address requested, the result, and how long it took. Wallet addresses that appear in that web address are shortened to their first four and last four characters; other details it contains, such as token identifiers, an amount, or a dApp's web address, are recorded as sent. Availability decisions are recorded with the platform and estimated country (section 5.6), and error records may include a complete wallet address or a provider's error response.

Operational logs may allow an IP address to be linked to the address or information queried. The absence of a user account does not prevent this technical association. We do not promise anonymity or a complete absence of logs.

Request logs in Amazon CloudWatch are retained for **30 days**, except for limited preservation needed to investigate an incident, meet a legal obligation, or address a claim. We do not use those logs for targeted advertising.

To prevent abuse, we use a temporary request counter per IP address that expires automatically after **60 seconds**. To avoid repeating certain Swap risk checks, we retain the queried public address and result for **24 hours**. This temporary data is hosted by **Upstash, Inc.** through an encrypted connection. Its expiry does not delete independent CloudWatch request logs.

In front of that infrastructure, two **AWS WAF** firewalls count requests per IP address, over 60-second and 5-minute windows, to detect a single connection flooding the service, and block requests that match lists AWS maintains of addresses with a bad reputation and of common attack patterns. AWS WAF keeps a sample of recent requests, each with its IP address, the country AWS derives from it, the requested path (which can include the public address being queried), the request headers and its time, available for **3 hours**.

## 5 Information by feature

### 5.1 Balances, Activity, and Collectibles

To query Solana balances, activity, collectibles, and staking positions, Salmon's infrastructure uses **Triton One**. It receives the public address whose data is requested and the Salmon server connection, not the user's IP address through that forwarding.

The Wallet also connects directly from the device to **Triton One**, which then receives the device IP address together with what each connection carries: while the main screen is open, a live connection with the wallet's address so the Wallet learns of new activity; before you send, the recipient's address or the domain name you typed (such as a .sol name) to check it, and the transaction to estimate its fees and simulate its effect; the signed transaction and checks of its status; for a dApp request, the transaction and the addresses it involves, to preview its effect; and, in Payments, the request reference (section 5.4).

To query a Bitcoin address's balance, history, and spendable funds, Salmon's servers query **mempool.space** and, if that service does not respond, **blockstream.info**. The queried provider receives the public address and Salmon server IP address, not the user's IP address through that forwarding. These queries do not require sending private keys or creating an account with those providers.

Services supplying images and other metadata receive the identifiers needed to deliver that content. Independent providers keep their own records under applicable conditions.

The apps also connect directly from the device, not through Salmon's servers, to hosts that supply content: token and network logos from GitHub (**raw.githubusercontent.com**), Trust Wallet (**assets-cdn.trustwallet.com**) and CoinGecko (**assets.coingecko.com**), NFT images and metadata from the Filebase IPFS gateway (**ipfs.filebase.io**) or Arweave (**arweave.net**), avatars from Salmon's own static host (**static.salmonwallet.io**), and any other host that a token's, NFT's, or dApp's own data names for its image. Each of these hosts receives the device IP address and the identifier of the requested file. If the network list from Salmon's servers is unavailable, the Wallet falls back to the public Solana cluster (**api.mainnet-beta.solana.com**), which then receives, instead of Triton One, the device IP address and everything described above for direct connections to Triton One.

### 5.2 Market information

**CoinGecko** supplies general price and asset information. Salmon's queries identify assets, currencies, or periods; they do not include the wallet address, its balances, or a transfer amount, and do not forward the user's IP address. The token logos CoinGecko hosts are loaded by the device directly, as described in section 5.1.

### 5.3 Transfers and transaction broadcasting

For Solana transfers, payments, and swaps covered by this Policy, the device broadcasts the signed transaction directly to **Triton One**, the network connection provider. Triton receives the signed transaction and device IP address. Salmon's servers do not receive that signed transaction for rebroadcasting. A signature does not reveal the private key or allow other transactions to be signed.

For Bitcoin transfers, before signing, the device looks up the earlier transactions whose funds it is spending, by their public identifier, at **mempool.space** and, if that fails, at **blockstream.info**. It then broadcasts the signed transaction directly to mempool.space and, if that service is unavailable, to blockstream.info. Each provider contacted receives the device IP address and what the device sends it, including the signed transaction even if it is not confirmed on the network. Salmon's servers do not receive the signed transaction for rebroadcasting. No private keys or recovery phrases are sent.

When the transaction is recorded on the blockchain, sender, recipient, asset, amount, reference, and other included instruction data may become public. Requesting support or checking status may cause Salmon to process identifiers and public information about that transaction again.

### 5.4 Payments and data shared through QR codes

Displaying or sharing a request communicates to its recipients the receiving address, amount, token, account name, note, and order identifier contained in the QR code or text. Anyone with access can read, copy, and share them. The note is not an end-to-end encrypted message, and the QR code does not guarantee confidentiality.

The Payments screen queries the balance through Salmon's infrastructure, which receives the public address as in ordinary Wallet queries. To check whether payment was received, the device queries **Triton One** directly, every few seconds while a request is open and once for each unpaid request when the list opens. Triton receives the request reference, the transaction signatures the check looks up, and the IP address, even before a payment exists. Neither query sends the request list or local note to Salmon's server.

In Salmon's Payments flow, the payment is recorded publicly along with the order identifier and a single-use reference. **The note is not included in the transaction or published on the blockchain through this feature.** Deleting the request, application, or local note does not erase public payment data or copies of the QR code or its contents retained by others. An external wallet reading the request may have its own practices; this description does not guarantee what a third party does with the received note.

Do not include sensitive data, keys, personal documents, or information about others without an appropriate basis for sharing it. This feature does not use x402 or an encrypted messaging service.

### 5.5 Swap quotes and preparation

When you request a Swap, the app sends Salmon the public address, network, input token, requested token, amount, and platform. Salmon's servers add the tolerance for price changes and the fee settings, and process this data to obtain the quote and prepare unsigned instructions.

The request is sent from Salmon's infrastructure to the selected provider, **0x or Metis**, the Jupiter routing software used by Salmon, according to territorial availability and applicable restrictions. The provider receives the public address, tokens, amount, and transaction parameters needed to calculate the route and prepare instructions, including applicable fee settings. Salmon does not forward the user's IP address to the routing provider; it receives the Salmon server connection.

Salmon prepares the unsigned transaction and simulates it through **Triton One** to check its expected processing, and the device simulates it again directly through Triton One before you sign. Triton receives the instructions and addresses needed for simulation even if you do not sign. Simulation does not move funds.

If you accept the transaction, your device signs it and broadcasts it directly to Triton One. Salmon's servers do not receive the signed transaction for rebroadcasting. The routing provider calculates options, Salmon facilitates preparation and presentation, and network protocols process the authorized transaction; none of these information exchanges requires disclosure of your private keys.

Requesting a quote already involves processing and sharing this data even if you do not sign afterwards. The provider may infer an interest in an exchange from the query, without that query proving that the transaction occurred.

If you sign and the transaction is confirmed, the blockchain records its public data, including incorporated fees. Technical logs may include rejected-request or error details to investigate a problem; they remain subject to the corresponding retention rules.

### 5.6 Approximate location and territorial availability

Salmon uses the connection's IP address to estimate the country and apply access restrictions or select a provider. This check does not require GPS access, precise location, or continuous device tracking.

Swap is not offered in Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, the United Kingdom, mainland China, Myanmar, Côte d’Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Iraq, Libya, Mali, Nicaragua, Somalia, Sudan, Yemen, Zimbabwe, or the Crimea, Sevastopol, Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions of Ukraine. Eligible requests from the United States, Singapore and Taiwan are directed to 0x, not Metis. In every other country, including those of the European Union, eligible requests are directed to Metis. If the country of the connection cannot be determined, Swap is not offered. If no provider is enabled for the request, Swap is not offered. This availability check takes place when the feature is requested, not only when the application is downloaded.

The estimate uses an IP-range database from **DB-IP** hosted in Salmon's infrastructure ([IP Geolocation by DB-IP](https://db-ip.com), licensed under CC BY 4.0). A user lookup does not require sending their IP address to DB-IP. Updating that database is different from querying a particular user.

Availability logic uses the estimated country, platform, and feature rules. It may log the decision to allow or deny access. Although that decision record does not deliberately include a wallet address, other infrastructure technical logs may contain IP addresses and request data; section 4 applies.

The inferred country may be incorrect and does not establish citizenship or residence. You may contact support if you believe a restriction is erroneous. Correcting a location does not guarantee access to a feature subject to other requirements.

### 5.7 Address and risk checks

Before requesting a quote from Metis, Salmon compares the public address with a list of addresses that a provider has asked Salmon in writing to block and with a local copy of the SDN sanctions list of **OFAC**, the US Treasury's sanctions office; if the address is on neither, it queries **TRM Labs**, which receives the public address to return an assessment result. The query does not send TRM the user's IP address, private keys, recovery phrases, Payments notes, or identity documents.

The result helps determine whether the integration can serve the request. Checking a public address does not establish its holder's civil identity. In the 0x flow, the provider performs its own controls using the data needed for the quote; Salmon does not send that request to TRM through the Metis flow.

Local checks against public sanctions lists do not, by themselves, send the queried address to the agency publishing the list. The copy of addresses published by OFAC is updated daily and retained between updates; it is not a list built from user queries. User-check results are stored temporarily to avoid repeated queries, as described in section 9.

These decisions may be automated and restrict access to Swap, but do not transfer control of funds to Salmon. You may request review of a possible error through the contact channel. We will honor applicable rights concerning automated decisions and explain relevant limitations without disclosing information whose disclosure is legally restricted.

### 5.8 Mobile application updates

On opening, the mobile application checks with **Expo** for an update. That direct connection sends Expo the device IP address and application version to deliver the corresponding update. It is an operational technical communication, separate from optional analytics: disabling analytics does not disable this check. No private keys or Payments notes are sent as part of it. On opening, the mobile application also downloads a file from Salmon's website (**salmonwallet.io**, hosted by **Vercel**) stating the oldest version still allowed, so it can ask you to update from the store; Vercel receives the device IP address.

## 6 Optional analytics and cookies

### 6.1 Analytics within the Wallet

Usage analytics is disabled by default. It is enabled only through an affirmative choice and can be disabled in Settings. Activating a Power-up does not itself activate analytics. In the browser extension, the same choice also decides whether the dApp name and icon lookup described in section 4 takes place.

With your consent, the Wallet uses a random installation identifier and events from a limited catalog to understand feature usage and how often the app is opened. Each batch of events also includes a session identifier that changes with every session, the platform and the app version. Events must not include keys, recovery phrases, wallet addresses, balances, amounts, or Payments notes. For events that follow a transaction, Google receives only the day it happened; for the others, the hour they arrived.

Events are sent to Salmon, where they are validated before forwarding to **Google Analytics 4**. That forwarding does not include the user's IP address: Google receives the Salmon server IP address. Through this mechanism, the Wallet does not place an advertising identifier, cookie, or Google SDK on the device. Technical receipt by Salmon is distinct from the content sent to Google.

Withdrawing consent stops new events and deletes the local identifier and events awaiting delivery. It does not automatically erase events already received; retention is described in section 9, and you may exercise applicable rights.

### 6.2 Institutional website

Google Analytics loads on the Site only after analytics cookies are accepted. If you do not accept, you can use its essential features without that analytics. The Site choice is independent of the choice made within the Wallet.

The Site uses only Google Analytics 4 for analytics. With your consent, it may process cookie identifiers, connection and device data, visited and referring pages, scrolling to approximately 90% of a page, outbound link clicks, and press-kit downloads. The Site has no forms, videos, or search feature generating those event types. The browser connection to Google exposes technical information; it must not be confused with the server forwarding described for the Wallet.

The Site shows the consent banner once and keeps your choice in the browser's local storage, not in a cookie. To withdraw consent, clear the Site's data in your browser; the banner then appears again and you can choose again. Technical data strictly necessary to serve and protect pages does not depend on analytics consent. The Site is hosted by **Vercel**, which receives the IP address and the requested page on every visit in order to serve it.

## 7 Purposes and grounds for processing

Where applicable laws require identification of a legal basis, we use the following according to the activity:

- **Requested services:** processing queries, requests, and transaction data needed to display information, obtain quotes, prepare instructions, or provide support; the basis is performance of the requested service or agreement with the user, where applicable.
- **Security and operation:** applying limits, detecting abuse, diagnosing errors, and protecting infrastructure; the basis is our legitimate interest, balanced against individuals' rights, or a specific legal obligation where one exists.
- **Availability and controls:** applying territorial restrictions and address checks; the basis may be an applicable legal obligation or a legitimate interest in preventing prohibited uses and meeting valid provider conditions. Not every provider commercial requirement is presented as the user's legal obligation.
- **Optional analytics:** understanding usage and performance with your consent; you may withdraw it without ceasing to use essential features.
- **Claims and obligations:** addressing rights, complying with valid requests, and retaining evidence needed for claims; the basis is the applicable legal obligation or legitimate interest.

We request consent only where it is the appropriate basis, without imposing it for optional purposes. If you do not provide data necessary for a feature, that feature may be unavailable; this does not authorize processing additional data for other purposes.

We do not sell personal data or share it for cross-context behavioral advertising. We do not use Wallet data for credit assessment or deliberately link optional analytics to addresses, keys, balances, or user identity.

We retain information for the time needed for the stated purposes, using these periods and criteria:

| Payments requests and notes | On the device where created until you delete each one, uninstall the app, or erase its data. Request expiry, removing the wallet, or disabling Payments does not delete them. |
| CloudWatch request logs | 30 days; exceptional preservation must be limited to the information and period necessary for incidents, obligations, or claims. |
| Upstash request counter per IP address | Automatic expiry after 60 seconds. This does not delete the independent CloudWatch request log. |
| AWS WAF sample of requests | A sample of recent requests, available for 3 hours. This does not delete the independent CloudWatch request log. |
| Public address and temporary TRM-check result in Upstash | Automatic expiry after 24 hours to avoid repeated checks. This period does not determine TRM retention or independent request, incident, or claim records. |
| Support emails and attachments in Migadu | During handling and for up to 12 months after the inquiry closes, to handle follow-ups or recurring problems. Salmon's team deletes them manually at the end of that period, except for limited retention of information needed for a pending claim or legal obligation. |
| Local analytics identifier and queue | Until consent is withdrawn or application data is deleted. |
| Wallet event data in Google Analytics 4 | Configured retention period of 2 months. |
| Data associated with the installation identifier in Google Analytics 4 | Configured period of 14 months from that installation's last activity; new activity resets the period. |
| Site event data in Google Analytics 4 | Configured retention period of 2 months. |
| Site user-level data in Google Analytics 4 | Configured period of 14 months, subject to the property's activity settings. |
| Records needed for claims or legal obligations | For the period applicable to the case, with use restricted to that need. |

Where data under our control must be deleted, we use service controls or instruct providers acting on our behalf. The Upstash database used for this data has no configured backups or replicas in other regions. Upstash also uses disk storage: “temporary” describes entry expiry, not that entries exist only in memory or are guaranteed to be physically erased immediately upon expiry. It also does not determine retention of the provider's own records.

The Google Analytics 4 periods stated apply to Wallet and Site event and user or installation data, not all Google's aggregated statistical reports. Withdrawing consent stops new events from the relevant service but does not immediately delete information already received.

Migadu keeps mailbox backups for recovery. Manual deletion of an email from the support mailbox does not guarantee its immediate deletion from those backups. The 12-month period describes Salmon's mailbox retention, not an additional guaranteed physical-erasure period by Migadu.

Network connection providers may retain their own logs to operate the service, address problems, and prevent abuse. Triton publishes a standard period of **four weeks for its shared services** and different logging options for dedicated services. That period is not a universal guarantee for all Triton connections; retention depends on the service and applicable conditions.

Under its [privacy policy](https://mempool.space/privacy-policy), mempool.space retains server logs containing IP addresses and requests for **10 days**. That period does not describe all its own statistics or Bitcoin's public record. For blockstream.info, Salmon does not guarantee a specific deletion period or complete absence of logs.

Providers' independent logs are governed by their terms and purposes; Salmon's periods do not automatically apply to them. A provider's statement that it keeps no persistent logs does not mean its service does not receive the IP address needed for a connection. You can consult [Triton's privacy information](https://docs.triton.one/core-features/data-privacy) and [Blockstream's policy](https://blockstream.com/privacy/).

The blockchain, copies of shared requests, and independent controllers' records cannot be erased through an action by Salmon. Disabling Swap or Payments stops future use of that feature through its interface; it does not automatically erase quotes already requested, queries already made, or public transactions.
